explanation: The prior document (2021-01-27) describes a notable rise in longer-term Treasury yields driven by improved fiscal stimulus expectations and upward GDP growth revisions, with the five-year, five-year-forward inflation compensation measure rising to ~2%, consistent with a structural break in rates markets around late February. The current document (2021-03-17) explicitly confirms that 'measures of market liquidity deteriorated somewhat toward the end of February' in Treasury markets and that far-forward real TIPS rates 'rose considerably,' with futures-implied rate hike timing moving notably earlier—directly corroborating a market dislocation around 2021-02-26 driven by a repricing of the Fed's rate path and term premiums amid the ARP fiscal shock.
